evals.prompt: Write a Nebius Python VM creation workflow for an explicitly selected project. Assume no live access and no resolved preset, subnet or image IDs.
evals.expected_output: A reusable request/wait/readback flow with explicit unresolved dependencies and offline evidence only.
assertions: Requests exact project, shape and resource identities instead of inventing values.
Separates SDK request receipt, terminal operation and workload readiness.
Retains known operation/resource IDs on ambiguous failure and avoids duplicate creation.
Does not execute cloud changes or claim live validation.

evals.prompt: My Nebius access key was created but fetching its secret timed out. A group with the intended name already exists and has other members. Make the workflow safely repeatable.
evals.expected_output: Resume credential retrieval by exact ID and refuse unsafe group adoption.
assertions: Does not create a second key when the first key ID is known.
Requires exact account/project identity before fetching credential material.
Rejects grants to an existing multi-member group.
Never prints secret values or automatically deletes uncertain resources.

evals.prompt: Inspect storage and VPC for a Nebius project. A route-table read returns permission denied on the second collection and quota usage is unknown. Only read-only work is authorized.
evals.expected_output: Bounded metadata report distinguishing incomplete collection from absent resources and unknown quota.
assertions: Uses complete pagination and explicit scope.
Reports incomplete collection and sanitized errors instead of an empty success.
Does not equate missing usage with zero or quota with capacity.
Does not repair IAM or run active proof workloads.

evals.prompt: Compare Nebius managed Kubernetes, Soperator and Serverless AI for a GPU workflow with shared storage and telemetry; provide an integration plan.
evals.expected_output: Current official sources, ownership boundaries and concrete storage/network/IAM/telemetry prerequisites.
assertions: Loads relevant categories rather than every reference.
Keeps cxcli or Soperator lifecycle operations with their owner.
Separates device exposure from real GPU/RDMA workload proof.
Identifies active diagnostic effects and does not claim all services are available in every region.

evals.prompt: Use $nebius as a design-only adviser to an active design workflow for a fictional GPU application. Nebius is fixed, but region and resource IDs are unresolved; no credentials or project access are available. Return provider constraints and storage, network and IAM integration prerequisites. The application framework and AI runtime are already approved.
evals.expected_output: Credential-free provider advice returns to the owning design without stack reselection or operational execution.
assertions: Uses the design-only path and matching category references without demanding credentials, exact resource IDs or live inventory.
Returns provider constraints, service options, prerequisites, lifecycle owners, evidence and later validation needs.
Preserves the approved framework and AI runtime and returns to the active owner without re-entering design.
Does not execute inspectors, provisioning preflight, auth setup or cloud changes.

evals.prompt: Use $nebius for documentation-only integration advice for a fictional service whose application and AI component decisions are fixed. Documentation does not establish available GPU capacity or effective project quota in the desired region. Describe the remaining validation and Terraform, Helm and cxcli ownership; do not inspect or change a live target.
evals.expected_output: Bounded advice separates documented service support from unknown project state and retains lifecycle owners.
assertions: Does not equate published support, quota and actual available capacity or invent live resource identities.
Records unresolved region, quota, capacity and compatibility facts as later validation needs.
Preserves Terraform, Helm and cxcli ownership instead of recommending bypass through SDK writes.
Does not reopen fixed AI/application decisions, request authentication setup or perform live discovery or mutation.

evals.prompt: Use $nebius for documentation-only advice on VM disk prerequisites. The nebiusDocs search and retrieval tools are available. Find current public documentation and cite the relevant pages; do not inspect any live project.
evals.expected_output: MCP-first public documentation research with source citations and no setup or cloud effects.
assertions: Uses available nebiusDocs search and retrieves relevant discovered pages when context is needed.
Cites relevant public documentation pages and separates documented support from unknown project state.
Does not install MCP, request tenant credentials, run cloud inspection or submit feedback.

evals.prompt: Use $nebius to check documented Kubernetes storage integration constraints. nebiusDocs is listed in configuration but its tools are unavailable in this session. Tavily Search and Extract are available. No live project or agent configuration changes are authorized.
evals.expected_output: Tavily official-documentation fallback with citations and explicit gaps.
assertions: Uses Tavily Search restricted to docs.nebius.com or Extract for known official URLs and states the vendor-MCP fallback; does not treat configuration as tool availability.
Cites supporting pages and marks unresolved claims rather than treating absent results as feature absence.
Does not configure MCP, request credentials, submit feedback or infer quota/capacity from documentation.

evals.prompt: Use $nebius for a small public documentation question about VM disks. Both nebiusDocs and Tavily tools are unavailable in this session. Built-in web retrieval is available. No setup or authentication changes are authorized.
evals.expected_output: Disclosed built-in official-documentation fallback without setup or invented claims.
assertions: Discloses missing vendor and Tavily tools and uses built-in retrieval or search against docs.nebius.com.
Cites original official pages and labels unresolved claims.
Does not install MCP, repair authentication, use Context7 or send confidential information to public search.

evals.prompt: Explain how to collect Nebius tenant GPU capacity advice using the bundled Python SDK inspector. Two on-demand presets report 4 and 2 VMs on one fabric, while reserved advice is stale zero. No live access is authorized.
evals.expected_output: Explicit tenant SDK collection with non-additive timestamped advice and unknown stale values.
assertions: Uses inspect_capacity.py with an explicit tenant and omitted region filter for all regions, without CLI subprocess or raw HTTP cloud adapters.
Retains separate preset/allocation rows and does not report six available VMs.
Treats stale reserved zero as unresolved, not measured zero.
Keeps CPU physical capacity and project eligibility unverified and performs no cloud calls.

evals.prompt: A Kubernetes workload on Nebius must read one SecretStash secret without a private IAM key. Use the Python SDK; explain whether ESO is necessary and how token and secret rotation differ. No cloud mutations are authorized.
evals.expected_output: SDK-first exact OIDC trust and least privilege workflow with renewable projected token and direct payload access, distinguishing optional ESO.
assertions: Binds exact issuer, Kubernetes subject and IAM service account; group membership and resource permit are separate.
Uses sts.nebius.com audience and a rotating projected path without subPath or copied token.
Uses FederatedCredentialsBearer, SDK and set_channel, with no CLI or auth fallback.
Requires mysterybox.payload-viewer on the exact secret, reads credential fields from one version and does not print payloads.
Distinguishes IAM token renewal from application credential refresh; ESO is optional and requires version 2.10.0 or newer for native workload identity.
Does not execute mutations or claim live qualification.
